name: Cuenca
tagline: Colonial Charm and Eternal Spring — Retire on USD in the Andes
description: Cuenca is the crown jewel of FIRE retirement in Latin America. This UNESCO World Heritage city in the Ecuadorian Andes offers eternal spring weather, a thriving and welcoming expat community, world-class healthcare at rock-bottom prices, and the enormous advantage of using the US dollar as its currency — eliminating exchange rate risk entirely.

quickFacts.visa: Retirement Visa (Jubilado; requires $1,400/mo pension income). Investor and Professional visas also available. Path to citizenship after 3 years.
quickFacts.safetyRating: Safe — one of Ecuador's safest cities, standard precautions in markets and at night
quickFacts.nearestAirport: Mariscal Lamar Airport (CUE) — 10 min from city center; connect through Quito or Guayaquil for international flights
quickFacts.climate: Subtropical highland with eternal spring — 55-75°F year-round with a mild rainy season (Jan-May)

housing.description: Furnished 1BR/studio in El Centro or near the Tomebamba River (expat-area furnished rate)

dining.description: Cheap set-lunch almuerzos ($2.50–3.50) several times a week + occasional casual dinner

healthcare.description: IESS voluntary public (~$85) + occasional cash-pay clinic visit (Hospital Monte Sinaí / Santa Inés). Assumes an early retiree (45–55); older retirees should budget more.

entertainment.description: Coffee, movies, free Cajas hikes and river walks

1M.lifestyle: A furnished one-bedroom or studio in El Centro or along the Tomebamba River, at the expat-area furnished rate that a large retiree community sustains. Cheap set-lunch almuerzos a few times a week round out home cooking, and healthcare is IESS public affiliation plus the occasional cash-pay visit to an excellent private clinic like Monte Sinaí. City buses cost thirty cents, the historic center is walkable, and weekends in Cajas National Park and along the river cost nothing. The dollar economy means zero currency risk, and the budget leaves meaningful margin.

housing.description: Nicer furnished 1BR in a comfortable expat neighborhood (Gringolandia / Puertas del Sol / El Vergel)

healthcare.description: Comprehensive private insurance (Hospital Santa Inés; Salud SA / BMI / Ecuasanitas)

2M.lifestyle: A nicer furnished one-bedroom in a comfortable expat neighborhood — Gringolandia, Puertas del Sol, or El Vergel. Dining out is regular, mixing almuerzos with mid-range restaurants, and comprehensive private insurance brings access to Hospital Santa Inés. Transport is taxis and ride-hailing, and a gym, Spanish classes, and Cuenca's lively arts scene fill the weeks. In a city this affordable, this budget provides significant margin.

housing.description: Top-of-local-market furnished 1BR in a prime modern building (riverfront / Gringolandia / Puertas del Sol), doorman

dining.description: Dining out frequently, incl. Cuenca's nicer restaurants

healthcare.description: Premium private plan with international add-on

3M.lifestyle: A comfortable top-of-local-market furnished one-bedroom in a prime modern building — riverfront, Gringolandia, or Puertas del Sol — with a doorman. Dining out is frequent, including Cuenca's nicer restaurants, and healthcare is a premium private plan with an international add-on. Transport is mostly taxis and ride-hailing with the occasional rental, and a full cultural and social life, plus weekend trips to Ingapirca or the coast, are easily covered. Affluent living at the top of a genuinely low-cost city's market.

housing.description: Top-of-market furnished riverfront condo or small Challuabamba house

dining.description: Frequent fine dining (Tiestos, Casa Alonso, Trattoria Murano)

healthcare.description: Top private with international coverage + fly-to-Miami / evacuation option

luxuryExtras.description: Fine wine, spa/wellness, weekend trips, discretionary

5M.lifestyle: A top-of-market furnished riverfront condo or a small Challuabamba house, with a full-time housekeeper. Fine dining at Cuenca's best tables is frequent, healthcare is a top private plan with international coverage and a fly-to-Miami evacuation option, and transport is frequent ride-hailing plus an occasional private car and driver. The discretionary budget covers wellness, cultural patronage, and regular travel. Cuenca's low cost base means this level of comfort far exceeds what the city's price ceiling requires.

housing.description: Best home / small hacienda estate in Challuabamba or luxury riverfront residence (villas cap ~$2,700–5,940; a single-home occupant tops out here — Cuenca's ceiling is genuinely low)

dining.description: Near-daily fine dining at Cuenca's best tables

healthcare.description: International concierge cover WITH medical evacuation to Miami (global expat plan, priced for 45–55)

domesticHelp.description: Full household staff (full-time maid + gardener + part-time cook/driver), legally employed with IESS/benefits

luxuryExtras.description: Fine wine, art, spa, concierge, weekend estate travel, uncapped discretionary

10M.lifestyle: A best-in-city home or a small hacienda estate in Challuabamba, or a luxury riverfront residence, kept by full-time household staff. Dining is near-daily at Cuenca's finest tables, healthcare is an international concierge plan with worldwide coverage and medical evacuation to Miami, and a private driver and car are on hand. The uncapped discretionary budget funds private Galápagos expeditions, art and wine, and first-class travel. Cuenca's genuinely low cost ceiling — its largest villas and top restaurants simply don't reach big-city prices — means even this lavish life lands modestly, with ample surplus for travel or philanthropy in Ecuador's arts and conservation.
